name: Shotbase
tagline: Browser tool for turning raw app screenshots into polished App Store and Play Store marketing images.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This category is one of the purest one-shot targets there is: it is text, images and rounded rectangles composited onto a fixed-size canvas and exported as PNG. There is no network, no shared data, nothing that gets better because other people use it. An agent can produce a local tool with device frames, gradient backgrounds, headline text, per-store export presets and a zip download in a single sitting. What you will not get for free is the taste baked into the paid templates, and the store size tables that quietly change every year. If you ship one app a year, buy it or use the free tier; if you ship ten, own the pipeline.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you drop in raw screenshots, pick a device frame and background, add headline text, and export a zip of correctly sized store images.
requirements: Device frame PNGs with transparent screen cutouts, or plain rounded-rect frames you draw yourself
A current copy of Apple and Google screenshot size requirements
whatYouLose: Professionally designed templates, which is most of what you are actually paying for
Someone else tracking App Store and Play Store size and aspect ratio changes
Direct upload to App Store Connect, so you are back to dragging files
Localized text variants and bulk generation across ten languages without you writing that loop
Font licensing sanity: the paid tool ships fonts it is allowed to ship
moatNotes: The moat is design taste plus keeping up with store spec churn, not technology. Both are real, neither is a network.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because screenshot design is a chore you touch four times a year, and the paid tool hands you a template that already looks like a real product launch. Recreating that look yourself means making a dozen small design decisions badly. The subscription is a tax on not having taste on demand, and for most solo devs that is a fair trade until the day the export pipeline needs to run in CI.
notes: Canvas compositing is trivial; knowing what a good screenshot looks like is not. Budget your weekend accordingly.
prompt:
Build a local-only app store screenshot generator. Empty folder, no accounts, no backend, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable: Vite + React + TypeScript, Tailwind for UI, plain HTML canvas for rendering, JSZip for export. Everything runs in the browser. No server, no database, no uploads anywhere.

Core flow:
1. User drags in one or more raw screenshots (PNG/JPG). Files stay in memory, never leave the page.
2. Left panel: a list of slides, one per screenshot, reorderable.
3. Right panel: per-slide controls for headline text, subhead text, font size, text color, text position (top or bottom), background (solid color or two-stop linear gradient with angle), device frame on/off, frame inset and corner radius, and screenshot scale/offset.
4. Center: live canvas preview of the currently selected slide, rendered at the active export size and scaled to fit.
5. Export button produces a zip: one folder per selected device preset, PNG per slide, filenames like 01-iphone-6.9.png.

Export presets, hardcoded in a single presets.ts file with a comment saying to verify against current store docs: iPhone 6.9 inch (1320x2868), iPhone 6.5 inch (1242x2688), iPad 13 inch (2064x2752), Android phone (1080x1920), Android tablet (1600x2560). Rendering must be resolution-independent: draw from normalized layout values, not pixel constants.

Device frame: do not ship copyrighted device art. Draw the frame yourself on canvas as a rounded rectangle with a border, a bezel, and a clipped screenshot inside. Put frame geometry in one config object so it can be swapped later.

Also build:
- A theme concept: named presets that set background, fonts and text placement across all slides at once. Ship three: Dark Gradient, Clean Light, Bold Accent.
- Save and load the whole project as a single JSON file (images stored as data URLs), so work survives a reload.
- A headless render function shared by preview and export, so what you see is what you get.

Out of scope, do not build: App Store Connect upload, localization pipelines, video previews, cloud storage, auth, analytics.

Use a .env file only if you add anything that needs a key. It should not need one. Ship a README with run instructions and a one-paragraph note on where the store size table came from and how to update it.
